body.text: Phase Grating Mathematics

Pioneered by physicist Manfred Schroeder in the late 1970s, mathematical phase gratings use varying well depths separated by thin acoustic dividers. When an incident wave encounters these wells, the reflected wavelets exit with distinct phase delays, resulting in destructive interference along the specular axis and broad dispersion elsewhere.
